name: hot water

attributes.attribute: Irish lore said not to throw it out at night for fear of harm to the fairies
moved in the farmyard after dark and could be struck by hot water
threw used water onto the stones of the courtyard

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Hot water is a motif in Irish folk belief. Irish lore told against throwing hot water out at night. The fairy people, it was said, still lingered about the farmyard after dark. The hot water could strike and harm them. In the days before drains were built in cottage kitchens, the housewife threw the day's cooking and cleaning water onto the stones of the courtyard. The cry "Towards ye! Towards ye!" warned any fairy of the coming boiling splash. The same cry also kept any person, unseen in the dark, from a sudden drenching.

okr.objective: Document the hot-water motif and the Irish practice that guarded the fairies.
key_results: the warning against throwing hot water out at night.
Describe the wife's habit of clearing the courtyard with used water.
Note the cry that warned both fairy and person of the pour.
